messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: AUTO-PAGE to @sara (oncall) — Canary traffic group 'canary-v14' showing p95/p99 regressions on /v1/chat/stream. p95=480ms (baseline 220ms), p99=2.7s (baseline ~420ms). Error rate stable but streaming stalls observed (client-side timeouts). dashboard: https://dash.redwood/test/canary-v14
sara: reading. thanks. paged. I'm taking it — starting triage. any deploys in last 30m?
james: I kicked a canary shift ~18m ago to move 3%->12% for v14 encoder tweaks (kv prewarm + quant profile). nothing else.
kevin: looking at infra metrics — encoder gpu utilization is normal, but RPC latencies spiking between router->pod (tails). logs show repeated `stall: kv-resp-timeout` on a subset of nodes. grabbing logs now.
infra-bot: Canary rollout event: `release/encoder-v14` at 5211111080 by james. traffic ramp policy at 3%->12% over 20m.
sara: ok. possible causes: kv warmup, mux backpressure, or model kernel slow path. can we pin which pods are seeing stalls?
james: attaching quick dump from the canary pods: ```
pod-17: kv-lookup median 3ms, p99=2.6s
pod-23: kv-lookup median 4ms, p99=5ms
pod-17 logs: "kv lookup timed out after 2500ms"
```
kevin: that's the interesting bit — it's not uniform. pod-17 (same AZ) hitting disk-backed KV fallback. evictions earlier? checking cache hit ratio.
maria: CS says 4 customers reported websockets reconnects/timeouts since ~09:02Z. one on standard tier, others on small workload. not widespread but noticeable for streaming use cases.
sara: impact: streaming stalls on canary traffic only (so far). rollout is causing user-visible tail latency for a subset of requests. prioritize rollback if we can't mitigate quickly.
kevin: mitigation attempt 1: increase kv cache size on canary nodes (hotpatch) to avoid fallback. command run: `kubectl -n infra set env ds/kv-agent CACHE_TARGET=1200` — applying now.
infra-bot: Patch applied to nodes with label canary=true.
kevin: monitoring cache hit ratio... it increased for pod-17 from 62%->91% within 60s. p99 for kv-lookup dropped from 2.6s->12ms for pod-17.
james: nice. but I'm still seeing some streaming stalls at the router level. could be request multiplexing — running a quick config diff:
```
router.conf: max_inflight=1024 -> unchanged
mux.pool_size=64 -> unchanged
quant.profile=v14_fast -> enabled
```
sara: are any fallback/quantized kernels being selected dynamically?
james: yes v14_fast exposes a slow-path for long sequences. but our traffic mostly short. not expected.
ops-bot: Reminder: if rollback is needed, use playbook: `playbook/rollbacks/canary_traffic_shift.md` and page PL.
maria: CS update: notified affected customers with mitigation steps (increase client-side reconnect backoff). they're asking ETA.
sara: current plan: keep hotpatch for cache and monitor 2m. if p99 stays <500ms and streaming stalls stop, continue hold and halt further ramp. if not, rollback to v13 and cut traffic to 0% for canary.
kevin: 60s check: p99 overall now 490ms, streaming stall count down 88% vs peak. client reconnects reduced.
james: good signal. I'll pause the next ramp step (we scheduled 24m->30m). pausing in deployment system now.
infra-bot: Rollout paused by james at 5211112270.
sara: keep observing for 10m. if stable, we'll handback to oncall with notes. if we see recurrence, we initiate rollback at 5211112400.
maria: CS will hold messaging until handback. they asked to highlight root cause suspected (kv-cache warmup + kernel slow-path).
kevin: logs show one more pod experiencing fallback at 5211112302 — I bumped its cache and it recovered. overall tail looks much better.
sara: 10m check at 5211112322: p95=230ms p99=510ms, streaming stall alarms cleared. no new customer complaints since the patch. I'm marking incident as mitigated but keeping the thread open for postmortem notes.
james: will revert quant-profile toggles in a follow-up branch and add explicit kv prewarm in the rollout. also adding a canary-only autoscaler to avoid resource contention during ramp.
maria: CS: informed customers and offered temporary token credits for reconnect pain. they'll ask for postmortem with timeline.
sara: handback: oncall -> ops (kevin) at 5211112345. action items: (1) james to add prewarm + canary autoscaler (PR), (2) infra to add cache warmup step to rollout pipeline, (3) product/CS to prepare customer timeline. I'll include logs and the hotpatch commands in the postmortem. good job team :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> monitoring. severity: SEV3. root cause (suspected): kv cache cold pockets causing disk fallback + edge kernel slow-path interaction for v14. playbook items assigned.
